newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-COMPAGNONI UNABLE TO ESCAPE COMPARISON WITH TOMBA.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-COMPAGNONI UNABLE TO ESCAPE COMPARISON WITH TOMBA.

text.p: Bathed in brilliant sunshine under a pristine blue sky, Deborah Compagnoni savoured her second gold medal of the world championships on Sunday.
But, frustratingly, once again the 26-year-old Italian was forced to endure questions about her absent compatriot Alberto Tomba, who has still to arrive at the championships.
Compagnoni was clearly annoyed at being asked yet again who is the better skier of the pair.
"You keep asking me that question and I have answered it," said Compagnoni."I will tell you again, we are different. I have won medals in three disciplines and he has won the World Cup.
"And he has won 48 races. For many years he has been in the limelight and now I'm having my greatest season ever."
After winning the slalom on Wednesday and the giant slalom on Sunday, Compagnoni has been feted as the athlete of the championships, at least until Tomba arrives.

She has compared racing the giant slalom to playing beautiful music but resents talk that she is nothing more than an opening act, warming up the audience, until the 'La Bomba' rock 'n roll roadshow moves into town.
Following Compagnoni's slalom victory, 35,000 spectators, the largest audience of the championships, flocked to Sunday's race.
But the crowd is expected to more than double next Sunday when Tomba hits the stage for the championship finale, a night slalom.
While perhaps unfair, the comparisons are inevitable.
With her giant slalom win Compagnoni joined Tomba with five Olympic and world championship gold medals and matched his achievement of two titles in one championships.
Tomba may have won World Cup titles but, for the moment at least, Compagnoni is the only Italian to defend successfully a world title. Tomba has defended an Olympic title.

While bothered by comparisons to Tomba, Compagnoni appeared flattered when the discussion expanded to include other sports and talk turned to Fausto Coppi, who is remembered fondly by most Italian sportswriters as their greatest hero.

"To be compared to Fausto Coppi is beautiful but there are so many great champions that to compare is hard," blushed Compagnoni, who is now also believed to be Italy's highest paid women athlete earning over $1 million in endorsements and prize money.
A novice artist, Compagnoni spent part of her time between races relaxing by painting a landscape.
On Friday she said she painted the mountains and on Saturday she filled in the sky. On Sunday she completed her masterpiece with a second gold medal.
